questions.question:
Which two mathematical signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

Option 1) : × and –

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows : 106 ÷ 3 - 2 + 70 × 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ - 2 + 70 × 7 = 110

⇒ 35.33 - 2 + __**70 × 7**__ = 110

⇒ __**35.33**__ - 2 + __**490**__ = 110

⇒ __**525.33 - 2**__ = 110

⇒ 523.33 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : – and ÷

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows :

 

106 - 3 × 2 + 70 ÷ 7 = 110

⇒ 106 - 3 × 2 + __**70 ÷ 7**__ = 110

⇒ 106 - __**3 × 2**__ + 10 = 110

⇒ __**106**__ - 6 __**+ 10**__ = 110

⇒ __**116 - 6**__ = 110

**⇒ 110 = 110**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 3) : × and +

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows : 106 ÷ 3 + 2 × 70 - 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ + 2 × 70 - 7 = 110

⇒ 35.33 + __**2 × 70**__ - 7 = 110

⇒ __**35.33 + 140**__ - 7 = 110

⇒ __**175.33 - 7**__ = 110

⇒ 168.33 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : + and – 

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows :

106 ÷ 3 × 2 - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ × 2 - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**35.33 × 2**__ - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**70.66**__ - 70 __**+ 7**__ = 110

⇒ __**77.66 - 70**__ = 110

⇒ 7.66 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"– and ÷".**

• **If** and **whether** are frequently interchangeable, yet they have different applications.

__
 
• When two subjects are linked by words like '**along with**', '**together with**', '**as well as**', etc., the verb agrees with the first subject. Therefore, we use **is** or **was,** or **has** instead of **are**, **were,** or **have**.

 
 
• *Example- The director **along with** his wife **has** come to our house.*

• This is known as subject-verb-agreement of a sentence where the **subjects and verbs agree with each other in terms of number** (singular or plural).
 
• If the subject of a sentence is **singular** the verb of that sentence should also be **singular**.
 
• If the subject of a sentence is plural the verb of that sentence should also be plural.
 
• There are many subject-verb-agreement rules in English Grammar.
